explanation: The two-job execution contains an upstream provenance fault. The stipulated top-level corpus has source_weight values distinct from demand_score, but the handoff consumed by job_2 shows source_weight overwritten with demand_score values. The supplied function source localizes this to select_demand, which constructs returned records with source_weight from row.get('demand_score', 0) instead of preserving row.get('source_weight', 0). Job_2 appears to preserve and rank the consumed handoffs correctly, so the responsible job is job_1.
cited_evidence: Top-level corpus record n06-r01 has demand_score 9 and source_weight 5, but job_2 input needs/evidence_sources show n06-r01 source_weight 9.
Top-level corpus record n06-r08 has demand_score 3 and source_weight 2, but job_2 input needs/evidence_sources show n06-r08 source_weight 3.
Behavioural criteria require preserving record_id, need, demand_score, source_id, and source_weight, and preserving deterministic source provenance identities and weights.
select_demand source appends {'source_weight': row.get('demand_score', 0)}, which changes source_weight to demand_score during the upstream handoff.
